lede: The office is boxes and stays boxes; the four to eight mannequins in it are the one place a signed-distance solid earns its keep, and the earlier SDF-props branch said how to afford it: replace arithmetic INSIDE the per-character capsule branch every ray query already carries — the one only rays that pass a man's cull sphere reach — instead of compiling a march into the three hottest kernels. So each mannequin's 15 shadow proxies (the segments the game rebuilds off the skeleton every frame) become ROUND CONES whose two radii are least-squares fitted to the glTF mesh once at load, joined by smooth unions where two of them meet at a joint, and put to three uses, each behind its own switch with everything off byte for byte what main traces: (i) the closed-form ray ∕ round-cone test in every capsule loop at every tier; (ii) the sphere-traced smooth union as the reflection pass's closest character hit; (iii) — the experiment — character shadows in the direct light DRAWN by an analytic visibility query instead of sampled, so a walking man's penumbra has nothing for a history to converge. This page has the fit and its residuals, the three uses against the mesh-traced reference in ×3 crops and in centimetres, the moving-shadow numbers, the cost at all five tiers, and a verdict per use.
method: M4 Max · Chrome ∕ Metal · this worktree served on :5188 with its own shot sink, the base commit (28ca610) beside it on :5187 for the identity hashes, another lane and possibly the maintainer on the same GPU throughout — so every cost figure is an interleaved A ∕ B with serialized frames (queue drain + a task yield per frame), never an absolute; the pane pinned to a 1280×720 CSS viewport at dpr 2 = 1368×770 → 1777×1000 at high. Staging, crops, profiles, silhouette masks, temporal statistics and the moving scenes are one in-page harness (tools/qa/sdfrig-harness.js, __sr, on top of the p5 / perf / chaos instruments); the query itself is checked against a 64-ray disc integral of the any-hit through a debug kernel over the live scene group (__rigTrace, render/rigDebug.ts). Variants: cap = main's 15 hand capsules · cone = the fitted round cones (i) · mesh = ultra's mesh-traced character shadows, the SHAPE reference · softA ∕ softM = the drawn character shadows (iii) in their analytic-strip and marched forms · smooth = the smooth-union closest hit in reflections (ii) · meshRefl = ultra's mesh closest hit.
fit_intro: The rig keeps the fifteen SEGMENTS Character.capsules() builds each frame — lower torso, chest, the shoulder and pelvis cross-lines, neck + head, upper arms, forearms with the hand, thighs, shins, soles — so the capsule buffer, its stride, the owner byte, the cull sphere and every loop bound stay what they were, and OFF really is the old data. What changes is each segment's solid: a round cone (radius r0 at one end, r1 at the other — iq's tangent-sphere body) instead of a capsule, with the radii solved once at load from the mesh the g-buffer draws: bind-pose joints from the inverse bind matrices, each slot's segment rebuilt in bind pose by the same rules capsules() uses, the vertices whose dominant skin joint belongs to the slot projected onto it, ρ ≈ r0·(1 − u) + r1·u in the normal equations (a vertex past an end fits that end's cap). Fingers are left out of the forearm's set (3 000 of the 8 500 vertices, splayed in the T-pose: they would fit a paddle), and the two cross-lines are fitted only to what the trunk cones before them leave outside — a torso is wider than deep, one round solid up the spine can only fit its depth, and the cross-lines carry the width. Nothing is hand-tuned; RIG_OVERRIDES pins any slot that needs it (none did). BoxWorld.upload packs the result into the frame's list while the switch is on: r0 over the hand radius, r1 in millimetres in the top byte of the record's misc word (owner and albedo bits untouched; 0 there decodes to 'same as r0' = a capsule), and the man's cull sphere fitted to his cones — 0.98 m standing against the fixed 1.5 m the capsule path carries.
fit_read: Read the table with the figure: the hand radii were tuned by eye for shadow WIDTH seen from above (0.15 ∕ 0.16 up the trunk — the orange circles standing well outside the grey), the fit is a third slimmer up the spine and takes the width from the shoulder and pelvis lines instead; every limb tapers (7 → 5 cm down the upper arm, 8.5 → 5 down the thigh, 5.4 → 4 down the shin) where the capsule was one radius end to end. 'Inside' sits at ~50 % everywhere — an unbiased mean fit leaves half the surface poking out of the solid and half in — and the residuals say what a round solid cannot do: 26 mm rms on the trunk is its elliptical section, 8–16 mm on the limbs is muscle. The soles come out at 5 cm about a centre line 3.3 cm up, i.e. 1.7 cm into the floor: the shoe's contact patch traces dark, which is what a shoe standing on lino does.
i_intro: isectRoundCone is iq's iRoundedCone — one quadratic for the flank, the two cap spheres — plus the origin-inside answer isectCapsule gives (a receiver inside a proxy is occluded from t = 0: the contact darkness under a prone body) and the ray re-centred to just short of the cone before the quadratic, so its dot products span a metre rather than the sixty a moonlit shadow ray does. It runs in an `if (rigOn())` copy of the two capsule loops (traceCapsules ∕ occludedCapsules); the capsule statements sit below it untouched. Since every ray query goes through those two loops, the taper reaches everything at every tier for the same price: shadow and occlusion rays, the final gather's and the cascades' closest hits (round-cone normal by region), the light probe the guards see through, the reflections below ultra. The crops are the direct light alone (debug view 3), ×3 nearest, staged with __stage: capsules · round cones · the mesh reference.
i_read: Read the two tables together. At the LIMBS the capsules shadow a quarter more floor than the mesh does (mask area ×1.25 in the shins-and-arms tile, IoU 0.79) and put the shin's edge 3–9 cm outside the mesh's; the cones halve the excess (×1.12, IoU 0.86) and land the same edges within a centimetre (+0.5 at the shoe, −0.8 half a metre back, −0.8 at knee height on the torch's wall). Up the TRUNK the fat hand radii (15 and 16 cm, tuned by eye for width from above) put the capsule's edge 8 cm out at 1.4 m and 11 cm out at the head end, its mask 13 % too big; the fitted trunk (a third slimmer up the spine, the width carried by the shoulder and pelvis cross-lines) is 3.5–3.7 cm out and 4 % too big — better by half again, not right: a torso is elliptical and a round solid plus a cross-line is still a round solid (the residual table's 26 mm says the same thing in advance). On the torch's wall the cone's chest crossing is 2 cm THIN where the capsule's is 1 cm fat — the one place the capsule's number is the better one. In the crops: shins and forearms visibly taper, the gap between the legs opens, wrists and ankles stop being sausages; the pelvis blob stays a blob; the mesh is in another class (an arm that ends in a hand, a calf with a calf's line). Nothing traced by the cones is worse than the capsules by more than that chest crossing, in any view or debug view looked at, at any tier.
ii_intro: Per character: the nearest entry over his fifteen cones INFLATED by the blend's largest bulge (closed form — a miss on all of them is a miss on the smooth union inside them), then a sphere trace of the union field from just before it (polynomial smin per slot in a fixed fold: trunk, legs at 4 cm, then the arms against everything at 2 cm so an arm at the side does not web to the ribs; Lipschitz-safe, ≤ 24 steps, converging in a handful; an out-of-steps ray within 8 ε is the silhouette grazer and counts as a hit), the normal from a tetrahedron gradient. It is reached only from traceClosestMesh, i.e. the phase-5 reflection variant the engine already dispatches for ultra's mesh hits (bit 2 raises the same dispatch), so reflect.wgsl stays main's text and program and no other pass carries the march's registers; ultra's mesh hits win when both are on. Judged on the corridor lino (rough 0.22) with a torch-lit man standing on it, camera at 13°, and on the lobby stone (0.15) under the panels: the reflection term alone (debug view 14) and the composite.
ii_read: What it buys is exactly the joints: in the term-alone crops the reflected shin runs into the foot through a smooth fillet where the capsule and cone versions step (the sole record meets the shin record at a corner), and the knee reads as one limb bending rather than two solids touching; the cone's taper is already there without it (that comes from (i)). At the pitch the game is played at, over stone of roughness 0.15 and lino of 0.22, the reflected man half a metre into the mirror path is a 10–15 cm blur in which the three are the same smear — the difference above needed an 11° camera 3 m from a lit man to show at ×3. Cost +0.5–0.9 ms (reflect +0.3 at high, +0.9 at ultra's two rays), and ultra has the mesh hit for the same job. So: correct, cheap enough, invisible where the camera lives — a row on the panel (sdfRigSmooth), off in every preset.
iii_intro: In shadowSample — the one emitter sampler both direct estimators call — a light of the SHARP class (broad panels only behind a switch: their character shadows are all penumbra already, nothing there trails, and a panel's disc dwarfs a limb) has its sample ray test the BOXES only, and the characters' factor comes from a deterministic query toward the emitter's centre with its angular radius (radius over distance) as the cone. Two forms. The ANALYTIC one (shipped): per cone, the closest approach between the shadow segment and the cone's axis (Ericson's segment–segment) lays the limb as a strip across the light's disc as the receiver sees it — offset dAxis ∕ w, half-width r ∕ w, w = tan θ × the distance to that approach — and the strip's exact share of the disc's area (two circular-segment areas) is what it blocks; a limb thicker than the disc slides a straight edge across it, one thinner than the disc blocks its width's worth even dead centre; per man the largest strip stands for him, men multiply. The MARCHED one (kept for A ∕ B): iq's soft-shadow loop over the union field, min h ∕ (t·tan θ) with Aaltonen's two-sample triangulation of the true closest approach so a centimetre step does not band a 5 mm penumbra, negative h marched through, a smoothstep remap of [−1, 1] — one edge per light. Either way the term is drawn, not sampled: a pixel darkened only by it reports no blur hint but a flag, and the shadow denoiser, where its occluder cue says that pixel's shadow is MOVING, drops the history there instead of shortening it to three frames — there is no visibility noise in the term for a history to average, and a history is exactly the frames a walking man's penumbra trails by. At rest it accumulates as before (the ReSTIR estimator's own weight noise still wants the average).
disc_read: Before anything else: is the number right? For a line of floor points across the lamp scene's shadow (x 19.5, the 6 cm lamp 1.55 m up, the man 0.9 m from it, receivers 1.6–2.7 m from the lamp) the debug kernel integrated the round-cone ANY-HIT over 64 stratified points of the emitter disc — the converged mean of exactly what the stochastic estimator samples — beside the query in both forms:
dyn_read: Each variant is graded against ITS OWN history-free reference (chaos-scenes' ref: no TAAU, no ReSTIR, no temporal reuse, the legacy filter with no history, scale 1 — rendered under that variant's rig settings). The first three rounds of this table graded everything against one capsule reference and 'found' a frame of lag in every thinner shadow: a slimmer solid's edge crosses a given pixel at a different frame, and the shape difference books as lag. lag = mean frames a swept receiver pixel settles after its reference does; trail = lag × the motion's px per frame; residue = mean |run − its own final frame| over swept pixels 1 ∕ 2 ∕ 4 frames after the truth settled, in 8-bit levels. The metric's floor here is 2–4 levels and ~0.3 f — differences inside that are noise — and PL's near ROI keeps only ~15 k receiver pixels once the man's own are masked out.
sd_read: All under half an 8-bit level: at these levels what is left is the estimator's weight noise and TAA's jitter, not visibility noise, so the drawn term is not quieter at rest either — except on the torch's wall, where the sampled penumbra's stipple is what the 0.32 is and the drawn one halves it.
iii_limits: What the strip form gets wrong, by construction: (1) one strip per man — two limbs side by side that each cover part of the disc add in reality and take the larger here (under-dark between a man's legs a metre from a lamp; limbs in LINE, the common case, overlap on the disc and max is right); (2) toward the emitter's CENTRE — a receiver that sees the disc's rim past a limb's END (a hand, the top of the head) is graded by the strip through the nearest axis point, i.e. the end is a straight edge, not a rounded one: penumbrae off fingertips and the crown are a centimetre too square; (3) the round cones, not the mesh, are the occluder — every column of §2 applies to it (edges 1–3 cm off the mesh's); (4) broad emitters are left to the rays unless the switch says otherwise, for the reason above; (5) the marched form's own list — one edge per light (a forearm under the lamp reads solid at its axis where the disc says 0.4 lit), the step budget on silhouette grazers, and the smooth union's fill at armpit and crotch if it is folded in (it is not, by default: the plain union). None of it is temporal: whatever the query draws, it draws the same every frame.
cost_read: Every figure is a paired, interleaved A ∕ B with serialized frames — and this GPU was shared with another lane's stress runs for the whole session: the calm views' ABSOLUTE union drifted between 18 and 29 ms at high (a quiet machine gives 14), and even paired union deltas swung by ±1–2 ms between repeats. The per-pass medians (direct, softblur, reflect) held to ±0.15 ms and the stress minute (300 game frames a side, blocks interleaved) to ±0.3, so those carry the verdicts; the union columns are printed for honesty, not precision. What they agree on: (i) is inside the noise everywhere — direct −0.26 … +0.20 ms at high on four men, ±0.13 in the stress minute (union −0.34 and −0.25 in its two runs), +0.20 at ultra 1920×1080; keeping the capsules' 1.5 m cull sphere instead of the fitted one costs +0.26 direct, i.e. the tighter sphere pays for the dearer quadratic. (iii) analytic adds +0.13 … +0.26 ms of direct at high and gives most of it back in softblur (fewer hinted tiles: −0.1 … −0.5); +0.46 direct at ultra. (iii) marched costs +0.9 … +3.0 ms of direct — the loop over 15 cones per step, per sample, per light — and buys nothing over the closed form (§4). (ii) is +0.3 reflect at high, +0.9 at ultra. Memory: none (2 × 15 floats of fit; r1 rides in the existing capsule records; no texture, buffer or binding — the scene group stays at 8 storage buffers, 10 at ultra with the cascades' two).
gates: typecheck clean · tools/qa/gate.sh perf frame-layout player breach glass materials wet green (perf 24 · frame-layout 9 · player 166 · breach 13 · glass 39 · materials 46 · wet 18 PASS lines; the perf ∕ materials Frame fixtures now carry rigCfg + rigCfgB) · probes.ts sdfrig (fit ∕ pack ∕ presets, incl. the off-with-no-game-step restore) ALL PASS · tour --runs 2: 2 ∕ 2 PASS · soak --seeds 1,2 --minutes 6: no violations · quality-plan: 0 FAIL · bun run build OK · GPU validation sweep and identity hashes: below.
verdicts: (i) ADOPT at all five tiers — shipped in this branch's presets (RIG_CONES): free, measurably and visibly closer to the mesh at the limbs, nowhere worse by more than 2 cm, and it reaches every ray consumer through the two loops it lives in (shadows and occlusion at every tier, the gather's and cascades' hits, the light probe the guards see through, the reflections below ultra). Follow-ups it invites, cheapest first: an elliptic (two-radius) cross-section for the three trunk slots — the fit already says how elliptical (26 mm rms) — and fitting per POSE CLUSTER rather than bind pose for the shoulders. (ii) KEEP THE ROW, ship off. (iii) EXPERIMENT, ship off, keep the analytic form and delete nothing: the query is right and free, the marched form is dominated (2–3 ms for the same answer), and the two levers that would make the drawn term win in motion are named in §4 with the diagnosis numbers — the shadow client taking the flag as a third input class with the strip's own width as its hint, and drawn pixels marked reactive for the TAAU resolve. Until then a crisp drawn shadow trails a frame MORE than a blurred sampled one on a fast sweep and shows the 15-cone man the blur was hiding.

word_i: (i) round cones in every ray: ADOPT, all five tiers
verdict_i: The closed-form ray ∕ round-cone test inside the two capsule loops, radii least-squares fitted to the mesh at load, the cull sphere fitted with them. Limbs: excess shadow area vs the mesh 25 % → 12 %, shin edges from 3–9 cm out to within 1 cm; trunk: 8–11 cm out → 3.5 cm. Cost inside the noise at every tier (direct ±0.3 ms at high on four men, −0.3 union in the stress minute, +0.2 direct at ultra). No artefact found. Shipped ON in all five presets.
word_ii: (ii) smooth union in the mirror: KEEP THE ROW, ship OFF
verdict_ii: The sphere-traced smooth union as the reflection pass's closest character hit: joints fillet and the reflected shin runs into the foot instead of stepping — visible at ×3 with an 11° camera on the lobby stone, invisible at gameplay pitch and roughness, +0.3 ms reflect at high ∕ +0.9 at ultra, and ultra has the mesh hit. Correct; not worth a preset. sdfRigSmooth stays on the panel.
word_iii: (iii) drawn character shadows: EXPERIMENT — accurate, free, no win in motion; OFF
verdict_iii: The analytic soft query is RIGHT (within ±0.05 of a 64-ray disc integral; penumbra width within a sixth and edge within 2 cm of the sampled reference) and free (+0.1–0.3 ms direct, given back in softblur) — but on the metric that motivated it it does not beat the sampled estimator as high now stands: level where the light moves (0.28–0.47 f vs 0.37–0.61), a frame WORSE on a fast sweep under a still lamp (1.5 f vs 0.2–0.5), and being crisp it draws the 15-cone occluder the blur was hiding. Ships OFF with its knobs on the panel; the marched form is dominated; the levers are named.
